transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm just... having some issues lately. 

It's mostly some nights, usually after work or... I don't know, maybe after a tense dinner. I just start eating, and... it's hard to explain. It feels like the decision-making part of me just shuts off. Like I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but I just... I can't make myself stop.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to make up for the food you ate?

...Yeah. I guess... sometimes. 

Usually it's late, like when everyone else is in bed. I'll... go to the bathroom and... well, make myself throw up. Or maybe take some laxatives. I just... I tell myself it's to undo the damage. 

It's... I don't know. I feel pretty embarrassed about it, honestly. And just... kind of shaky afterward.
How often would you say you've been making yourself vomit or using laxatives after these eating episodes—like, in the past week or so?

Um... I'm not really sure about just this past week. But... I guess for the last few months, it's been happening most weeks. 

Whenever I have one of those out-of-control nights, I just... I try to make up for it. By throwing up, or taking the laxatives. Or sometimes I'll just skip meals the next day... or force myself to go on a really long walk. Just... whatever I can do, I guess.
How often do you feel like you're having these out-of-control eating episodes where you can't stop yourself from eating, even when you want to?

Um... well, like I just said, I guess. It's... most weeks. For the last few months, anyway. 

The eating part happens, and then... I do the other stuff I mentioned to try and make up for it. They kind of just go together.
Can you describe what happens during one of these out-of-control eating episodes? Like, how much you eat and whether it feels like you can't stop once you start?

Um... I don't know. It's just a lot of food. 

Like... if it's a bad night, I might start with a whole plate of whatever leftovers we have. And then... I just keep going. I'll stand in the kitchen and eat bread, or whatever snacks are around. Ice cream. All of it in... maybe an hour or two. 

It's just... a lot. Way more than I'd ever eat if... if someone else was in the room with me. Once I start, I just... I don't really stop until it's gone.
Do these eating episodes or the things you do afterward cause you a lot of distress or affect your daily life in any way?

Um... I don't know. I mean, I'm still showing up for my cashier shifts. I handle my responsibilities at work just fine, so it's not affecting that. 

But... I guess I have been avoiding some family meals lately. Or if I am there, I'm just... kind of distracted. Because I'm just sitting there worrying about what I already ate, or... what I'm going to have to do later to make up for it. So... yeah. A little bit, I guess.
Can you tell me if these eating episodes always happen in a single, short period of time—like within a couple of hours—or if they can stretch out over a longer period?

Um... I think I mentioned that a minute ago. It's usually just... within an hour or two. Like I said before, with the leftovers and the snacks in the kitchen. It just happens fast, all at once. It doesn't really stretch out all day or anything.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating—like you can’t stop eating or can’t resist the urge to keep eating, even if you wanted to?

Um... yeah. I guess that's... kind of why I finally came in. 

It usually happens after work, or... maybe if dinner was really tense. I'll start eating and... it's like the decision-making part of me just shuts off. Like, I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but... I just can't make myself stop. So... yeah. I guess I do.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives even when you haven't had one of these out-of-control eating episodes?
No... I don't do that. It's really just... after those times I just mentioned. When I eat too much and can't stop. I don't do it... otherwise. Just then.
